facts.text: The bar-shouldered dove is a long-tailed dove native to Australia and southern New Guinea.
facts.quote: The bar-shouldered dove (Geopelia humeralis) is a species of long tailed dove native to Australia and Southern New Guinea.

facts.text: It sings a distinctive and melodious "cook-a-wook" or "coolicoo".
facts.quote: Its voice is a distinctive and melodious "cook-a-wook" or "coolicoo".

facts.text: The dove has a blue-grey breast with chequered brown-bronze wings.
facts.quote: The dove has a blue-grey breast with chequered brown-bronze wings.

facts.text: The feathers on its nape are striated and copper in colour.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the nape feathers are copper in colour.

facts.text: Its eye ring is usually grey but turns red-brown when breeding.
facts.quote: The eye ring tends to be grey but red-brown when breeding.

facts.text: It feeds on seeds on the ground, often in pairs, groups or large loose flocks.
facts.quote: Doves are often found in pairs, groups or large loose flocks and are seen commonly feeding on the ground feeding on seeds.

facts.text: Its flight is direct and swift, and its wings whistle while the birds are in flight.
facts.quote: Flight is direct and swift and wings whistle while the birds are in flight.

facts.text: In the south it breeds from September to January, and in the north from February to April.
facts.quote: Breeding season is from September to January in the south and February to April in the north.

facts.text: It lays two white, glossy and rounded eggs in a flat twig and grass platform nest.
facts.quote: Its nest is a flat twig and grass platform usually in trees and shrubs, mangrove or scrub.  The dove will lay two, white, glossy and rounded eggs.

facts.text: It prefers thick vegetation near water, such as damp gullies, mangroves, swamps and river margins.
facts.quote: Bar-shouldered doves are usually found in thick vegetation where water is present, damp gullies, forests and gorges, mangroves, plantations, swamps, eucalyptus woodlands, tropical and sub-tropical scrubs and river margins.
